passage:
I'm Minakshi, and being in the middle is funny. Everyone is very nice to you, right until they aren't.

Last term Bhavna and Deepa stopped speaking over a borrowed laptop charger, or really over what the charger meant. Bhavna sat on my bed one night and said, "You saw how she treated me, right?" The next day Deepa cornered me: "Tell me what she said about me." My stomach twisted, because part of me wanted to please whoever was in the room.

I told each of them the same thing. "I won't carry messages. I care about you both, and honestly the charger seems small next to the friendship, but I'm not going to pick a side." Bhavna stormed off. Deepa called me useless. It hurt 😔.

A month later they each told me, separately, that they trusted me because I never repeated what they'd said.

qa.q: What did Bhavna and Deepa stop speaking over?
qa.a: A borrowed laptop charger, or really what the charger meant.

qa.q: Why did Minakshi's stomach twist when each friend asked Minakshi to take a side?
qa.a: Part of Minakshi wanted to please whoever was in the room, even though Minakshi knew not to carry tales.

qa.q: What could someone in Minakshi's position say when both friends want them on their side?
qa.a: Say kindly that they will not carry messages or pick a side, keep their own view, and stay warm to both.

qa.q: Why might Bhavna and Deepa have trusted Minakshi later?
qa.a: Because Minakshi never repeated what either had said, each could tell Minakshi would not repeat their words to others either.

grounding: Two friends fall out and both want Minakshi on their side; Minakshi refuses to carry tales and stays kind to both.
